normative_action: HTTP status codes/transport semantics belong to the API layer; Application and Domain must not return IActionResult or status codes.
Choose 200/201/202/204 by actual HTTP semantics; no blanket 200, no 201 for internal inserts, no 202 for completed work.
A 201 response includes Location when a stable resource URI exists.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Location header requirement not in the oracle.

normative_action: By default a successful collection query with zero matches returns 200 with an empty collection, not 404.
401 for missing/failed authentication, 403 for authenticated but not permitted; 404 hiding requires a deliberate consistent policy.
409 for valid requests conflicting with current state; 412 when an explicit precondition such as If-Match fails.
Do not introduce API versioning merely because an API exists; add it for published compatibility or coexisting client generations.
Once relied on by external clients avoid silent breaking changes; a breaking change requires a new version or explicitly approved compatibility strategy.
Use one versioning strategy consistently; URL-segment is default unless requirements justify another.
Swagger/OpenAPI metadata describes the API that actually runs (routes, important statuses, schemas, authentication); no speculative responses.
Enable Swagger UI in Development by default; expose elsewhere only when deployment requirements explicitly justify it.
Health checks remain cheap and deterministic; no full business workflows or expensive/mutating database work.
Liveness must not depend on external dependencies whose unavailability could cause restart loops; readiness may depend on required capabilities and must reflect startup and dependency availability.
No secrets, credentials, connection details, stack traces or unnecessary diagnostics in publicly reachable health responses.

Dependencies point inward: Domain none; Application→Domain; Infrastructure→Application, Domain; Api→Application and Infrastructure only for composition/registration; inner layers never depend on outer; no Infrastructure-specific types in Domain/Application.
Domain holds business concepts independent of infrastructure/transport; simple entities are default.
Keep Domain independent of persistence technology, ASP.NET Core, HTTP, persistence and external-service concerns.
For CRUD/straightforward workflows keep entities simple and enforce rules in Application Services; validation, immutable fields, transitions or edit rules alone do not justify a Rich Domain Model.
Move behaviour into Domain only for non-trivial invariants benefiting from encapsulation; otherwise Rich Domain/DDD tactical patterns need explicit approval.
exceptions: Unless the approved specification requires it.

normative_action: No factory methods, private setters, transition methods, Aggregate Roots, Domain Events, Specifications, Domain Services, systematic Value Objects or similar merely to appear domain-driven.
Application Services are the default orchestration mechanism (coordinating Domain, repositories, external abstractions, UoW).
Define persistence/external-service abstractions in Application when use cases need them; keep infrastructure details out.
Application must not depend on persistence-technology types or ASP.NET Core transport types.
An oversized service is a signal to reconsider responsibilities, not an automatic reason to introduce another pattern.
Controllers are the default HTTP entry point and stay thin (bind/validate, invoke Application services, translate outcomes).
Controllers must not contain business logic, access the persistence session or concrete repositories, or construct infrastructure services manually.
By default Program.cs is the composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations.
Controllers do not consume Infrastructure implementation types directly.
Prefer specific repository interfaces for cohesive use-case persistence needs over table-mirroring generic CRUD contracts.
Define repository interfaces in Application and implement them in Infrastructure; query construction stays in Infrastructure.
Repository interfaces must not expose IQueryable<T>, persistence-technology types/query expressions or provider types; return materialized results.

Application must not depend on IGenericRepository<T>/generic CRUD contracts; a generic base exists only in Infrastructure to remove genuine duplication and must not replace the technology's query capabilities.
IUnitOfWork is the default commit boundary; repositories stage and do not commit; Application Services decide when to commit.
Infrastructure implements IUnitOfWork over the scoped persistence session.
Repositories in one use case share the same scoped Unit of Work and persistence session; inject repositories explicitly.
IUnitOfWork must not act as a repository container or service locator.
Keep cache technology out of Domain; no infrastructure cache APIs in Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.
Infrastructure translates remote HTTP responses into Application-facing abstractions; no HttpResponseMessage/transport concerns in Application.
By default registration stays near the owning layer; Api remains the composition root.
No separate Domain/persistence models merely for multiple API versions; version-specific contracts at the API boundary.
Do not duplicate equivalent DTOs across Api and Application merely for layer-shaped types; transport contracts when separation gives a concrete benefit.
Backend test projects get no broader production references than needed and keep inward discipline.
Follow existing conventions and .editorconfig; prefer modern C# when clearer; no rewrites solely for newer syntax; consistency over feature maximization.
For new code prefer file-scoped namespaces when consistent with the project.
By default one primary top-level type per file with matching file name.
exceptions: Small private/nested supporting types may stay with the owner.

normative_action: Do not reorganize an existing file merely to satisfy a preferred member ordering.
Task/ValueTask methods use the Async suffix by default; do not rename framework implementations or established APIs when that breaks a contract.

Primary constructors when DI/simple initialization stays clear; regular constructors when validation/initialization is non-trivial, explicit fields help, the codebase uses that style, or capture hurts understanding.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Constructor style criteria outside the oracle (EXC-002/EXC-003).

normative_action: Do not convert constructors mechanically.

Records when value semantics/immutability are desirable (many DTOs, genuine Value Objects); classes for identity/mutable lifecycle/inheritance/framework behaviour; not every DTO/Domain type becomes a record.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Record/class style rule outside the oracle.

normative_action: Keep implementation details non-public unless public API; use sealed for deliberate non-inheritance intent, not speculative JIT optimization.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Visibility/sealed conventions outside the oracle.

normative_action: Use modern features (collection expressions, pattern matching, switch expressions, target-typed new) when they read better; not when less obvious.
Use var when the type is obvious or unimportant; explicit type when clearer.

normative_action: Constructor injection is the default for required dependencies; avoid service-locator and property injection.
Never capture a shorter-lived dependency in a longer-lived service; singletons/hosted services needing scoped work create a scope per operation and resolve a scoped orchestration service.

Prefer strongly typed options for structured configuration; avoid scattered string IConfiguration lookups in services; direct IConfiguration belongs to composition/provider setup/infrastructure registration.
Validate settings at startup when missing/invalid values prevent correct or secure operation.
Use ILogger<T> with structured templates and stable property names; avoid interpolation.

Adding, updating or removing a NuGet/npm dependency follows the add-dependency workflow (version, deprecation, vulnerability, license checks).
Add a dependency only for a concrete current requirement; no hypothetical future use.
Use NuGet CPM: versions in Directory.Packages.props, versionless PackageReference by default, no duplicated versions in .csproj.
Keep package references in the narrowest project that requires them.
npm by default unless deliberately changed; maintain and commit package.json and package-lock.json; tooling in devDependencies unless there is a reason.

normative_action: Do not use exceptions casually for normal expected control flow.

Represent common expected outcomes (not found, transition not allowed, duplicate, concurrency conflict, rejected operation) explicitly when clearer, with the simplest contract (null, bool, typed outcome, deliberately adopted Result<T>).
Do not force a generic Result<T> pattern; it is not mandatory nor introduced project-wide because an operation can fail.
Application outcome categories use business semantics (Validation, NotFound, Conflict, BusinessRuleViolation), never HTTP-named categories.
Do not establish custom business exceptions as default architecture or throw/catch to jump between normal branches; typed exceptions for selected cases are a consistent project-level decision.
By default unexpected failures propagate to centralized handling (IExceptionHandler); avoid repetitive catch/log/rethrow blocks.
Catch an exception only to recover, translate into the layer's own outcome, perform a defined fallback, add context preserving the original, or perform required cleanup.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Closed whitelist of catch purposes is stricter than API-007.

normative_action: Never swallow exceptions to continue execution.
Log an unexpected exception once at the handling boundary, not repeatedly across layers and the global handler.
Expected outcomes such as not found or validation rejection are not logged as application errors.

By default ProblemDetails for non-validation failures and ValidationProblemDetails for request validation; keep the machine-readable contract stable and safe and never make human-readable messages the contract.
No stack traces, SQL details, connection strings, internal paths, secrets, raw exception messages or sensitive details in public API errors.
Normal client cancellation is not mapped to a generic 500 nor logged as an unhandled error.
Validate each concern at its owning layer; use FluentValidation for explicit request/use-case validation where appropriate.

API validates transport concerns; Application use-case/workflow rules; Domain genuine non-trivial invariants (not moved into FluentValidation for convenience); Infrastructure external-system assumptions.
Do not duplicate the same validation mechanically at every layer.
Modern standalone Angular APIs for new code organized by feature; no NgModules for ordinary new features.
exceptions: Integration or legacy dependency genuinely requires NgModules.

normative_action: Signals for synchronous local UI state, RxJS for async streams/HTTP composition/cancellation/event pipelines; avoid mechanical conversions.
Prefer functional interceptors for new code; keep them cross-cutting; no feature business logic in interceptors.
Avoid manual nested RxJS subscriptions; prefer composition operators.
Tie manual subscriptions from framework-managed code to the component/service lifecycle with current Angular facilities.
The frontend HTTP boundary is an @Injectable feature service using HttpClient.
The explicit form model for non-trivial forms is Angular Reactive Forms.
Feature-oriented structure: features own their UI and data access; no application-wide technical buckets or empty architecture folders; core/shared small.
Use shared only for genuinely cross-feature primitives; do not move feature code into shared merely because two components of one feature use it.
Pages/components focus on presentation and UI orchestration; do not move trivial presentation logic into services merely to shrink components.

Backend communication in explicit feature data-access services; no HTTP calls scattered through components; frontend API models match the published contract; no backend Domain entities in the frontend.
Follow the documented API error contract; centralize reusable ProblemDetails parsing when practical; do not infer business behaviour from human-readable messages.
Prefer simple component/service state before a state-management library.
By default route-level lazy loading for meaningful features; not every tiny component.
Use the explicit form model for non-trivial forms when useful; frontend validation is UX and never replaces backend validation or integrity/security enforcement.
Prefer clear correct code first; no specialized optimizations without a concrete reason; measurement/profiling for non-trivial optimizations.
Use async APIs for async I/O; never block with .Result/.Wait()/sync-over-async.
Propagate CancellationToken when meaningful; none on purely synchronous code without a use case.
By default TimeProvider for current-time-dependent logic needing deterministic tests; do not mechanically replace stored/explicit dates.
No HttpClient create/dispose per request; IHttpClientFactory or another long-lived strategy.
External I/O has bounded execution time; avoid overlapping unclear timeout mechanisms.
Retry only when safe; no automatic retries of state-changing operations without idempotency or duplicate prevention.
Respect Retry-After/rate-limit guidance where appropriate; no indefinite/aggressive retries.
Fallback only when semantically acceptable; never hide correctness failures behind defaults.
Caller cancellation is not a transient failure; not retried or converted into repeated attempts.
Filter/project in the database, avoid unnecessary round trips/over-loading, watch N+1, paginate potentially large results.
Caching only for clear measured/reasoned need with acceptable staleness; implementation per deployment/consistency/staleness; not merely because read frequently.
Every cache entry has a lifetime or explicit invalidation strategy.
Cache keys uniquely represent the value incl. identifier, tenant, user when user-specific, locale, query/filter parameters; no global keys for user/tenant data.
Invalidate/update cache only consistently with successful mutations; cache never a second source of truth.
Compiled queries, ValueTask<T>, pools, manual pooling, custom serialization, aggressive caching and raw SQL for performance only for measured/demonstrated need.
Do not sacrifice maintainability for speculative micro-optimization.
Prefer ordinary clear code; for demonstrated allocation-heavy hot paths consider spans/pooling/source-generated serialization/preallocated buffers and verify material improvement.
EF Core is an adapter-layer detail used directly with full capabilities; do not cripple repositories to preserve a generic abstraction.

Do not leak EF Core concepts into the use-case layer; persistence-technology types are DbContext/AppDbContext, DbSet<T>, EF APIs, EF-backed IQueryable<T>, query expressions and provider types; the persistence session is the scoped AppDbContext shared by repositories and UoW of one use case.
The repository boundary keeps persistence out of the use-case layer but does not hide EF Core from the adapter layer.
One SaveChangesAsync is the normal transaction boundary; no explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case needs more.
Maintain a small deterministic representative seed dataset for an empty Development database; readable deterministic examples over exhaustive/random combinations.
Seeding is an adapter-layer bootstrap concern and may use AppDbContext directly without repositories/UoW.

Substantial seed construction lives in a dedicated internal DbSeeder exposed via a narrow adapter-layer initialization extension, not Program.cs, AppDbContext configuration, entity configurations or migrations.
Automatic seeding only in Development; never seed Production automatically.
Tests own their setup and do not use the development seeder.
The seeder must not call Database.Migrate(), EnsureCreated() or create/upgrade schema; migrations applied separately before seeding.
Leave existing representative data unchanged; no seeder-based synchronization/repair/upgrade/overwrite/recreation; developers recreate explicitly.
Seed entities preserve current Domain invariants and valid relationships.
For provider fidelity the actual provider is SQL Server; EF Core InMemory is a different non-relational provider.

appsettings.Development.json provides a usable local connection string without secret credentials (e.g. LocalDB integrated security); credential-bearing values via user-secrets or another approved local mechanism.

Physical structure follows responsibilities: no speculative projects, infrastructure, empty trees or generic Common/Helpers/Utils buckets; create directories/projects only with meaningful cohesive content.
Never hardcode/commit real secrets, credentials, private keys, tokens or production connection strings, including example configuration.
By default local secret mechanism (dotnet user-secrets) in development; environment injection/managed store when deployed; no cloud-provider assumption.
Treat data from outside the trusted boundary as untrusted and validate it at the owning layer when assumptions matter.
Parameterized database access; never concatenate untrusted input into SQL.
Authorization enforced on the server; client guards/hidden buttons are UX only.
Anonymous access deliberate and visible; global/fallback policies, attributes or endpoint configuration; no redundant [Authorize] under a secure global policy.
No custom token/password security, hashing or reset-token crypto when ASP.NET Core/Identity covers it.
Validate issuer, audience where applicable, signing authority and lifetime for Bearer/OIDC; never disable validation to make a token work.
No authentication-failure detail revealing secrets/account state; avoid account-enumeration leaks.
With automatic browser cookie credentials include CSRF protection; the frontend framework does not remove the risk.
Do not claim one token-storage mechanism is universally secure; choose by threat model.
Production sensitive traffic uses TLS respecting hosting topology (no HTTPS-redirection requirement when the deployment provides secure transport); never disable certificate validation.
No custom cryptography when a reviewed platform mechanism fits; Data Protection is not universal database encryption.
By default the narrowest CORS policy for actual browser clients; never credentialed requests with unrestricted origins.
Never log passwords, tokens, private keys, auth secrets or full payment credentials; avoid PII without permitted need; log level does not make data safe.
No arbitrary request bodies, domain objects or sensitive payloads in logs by default; minimum useful non-sensitive context.
By default security-sensitive checks fail safely, not converting lookup/configuration failures into success.
Prefer visible startup/configuration failure over insecure fallback for required security controls.
Do not trust client file metadata such as MIME type as authoritative.
By default production containers use an appropriate runtime image, not SDK; do not switch to root to bypass permission problems.
NUnit is the default framework; follow an established other framework; no second framework without a concrete reason.

Tests verify observable behaviour and survive refactoring; no dependence on private methods, call sequences, implementation classes; no reproduced algorithms.

normative_action: For small finite spaces prefer explicit declarative cases over loops/branches/LINQ/generated machinery; state expected results instead of computing them.

Deterministic, order-independent tests isolated from Production/Development data, uncontrolled external systems and shared mutable state; no wall-clock reliance when TimeProvider can help; never connect to Production data.
Tests start from a known state, own setup, and do not depend on development seed data or execution order.
Coverage is diagnostic; no low-value tests to raise coverage percentage.

normative_action: SPECIFICATION.md is authoritative for project-specific functional requirements and observable behaviour when non-empty.
Do not silently weaken, contradict or materially extend approved behaviour or invent user-visible behaviour, rules, restrictions, limits, defaults or workflows.
If an omitted detail materially affects observable behaviour propose the smallest reasonable option and ask for approval.
Routine internal implementation choices that do not change observable behaviour need no approval.

Observable string semantics (case, collation, culture/ordinal, normalization, trimming, uniqueness, lookup) are product behaviour; when undefined and material ask for approval instead of choosing silently.
exceptions: Only when approved sources do not define them and the choice is material.

normative_action: CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md holds approved project-level tunable limits/defaults; SPECIFICATION.md owns behavioural intent.
SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contradict; on apparent conflict stop and ask which to correct.
Do not silently invent a material tunable value; propose with reason, get approval, record and synchronize.
Synchronize tunable value changes through the custom-settings workflow.

Never store secrets, environment-specific connection details, package versions, HTTP status codes, ports, migration identifiers, incidental constants or un-overridden framework defaults in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
Product and task inputs are not instruction layers: they may request an engineering decision change but never silently override engineering policy; a conflicting request becomes a Decision Request.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Precedence of engineering policy over product/task inputs is not entailed by GOV-001 (which concerns product behaviour authority).

normative_action: Prefer simple maintainable solutions; keep complexity proportional; avoid speculative abstractions.
Do not introduce frameworks, libraries, infrastructure or architectural patterns without a concrete current need.
Keep changes focused and preserve existing behaviour unless the task or approved specification requires change.

Before implementing a questionable request identify material concerns (duplication, cohesion, triggering/loading, context cost, conflicts, complexity) and propose an alternative; never silently rewrite or ignore the requirement.
Decided items (instructions, imported decision records, approved spec, established structure, accepted ADR) are followed and not reopened without approval.
Delegated decisions (local, reversible, no material boundary/dependency/convention/contract/behaviour change) are decided without asking.
Reserved decisions require explicit approval; the list is a minimum ('at least').
